previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and cough, initially concerning for pneumonia. Imaging revealed diffuse pulmonary opacities, but rapid improvement on repeat X-ray indicated pulmonary edema rather than infection. She was found to have culture-negative peritonitis, with elevated peritoneal fluid white blood cells that decreased with antibiotic therapy. A clogged PD catheter required one session of hemodialysis before resuming peritoneal dialysis, which successfully reduced fluid overload. Antibiotics were transitioned to intraperitoneal vancomycin and ceftazidime for completion as an outpatient. Orthostatic hypotension was managed with midodrine and florinef. She improved clinically, with resolution of respiratory symptoms and stabilization of volume status, and was discharged home in stable condition.

ACUTE/ACTIVE ISSUES:
====================

# Orthostatic hypotension
Patient diagnosed with orthostatic hypotension on recent 
admission. Likely secondary to autonomic neuropathy due to 
underlying type I diabetes mellitus, with possible contribution 
from polypharmacy. Commenced on midodrine 5mg daily and 
fludrocortisone 0.05mg on discharge. Continued issues with 
dizziness, both when sitting and standing, but worse when 
standing and walking. Patient unable to partake in normal ADLs 
because of this. Despite uptitration of midodrine dose in the 
time between discharge and this admission, there was minimal 
improvement in symptoms. On admission, orthostatic vital signs 
were; 125/65 (lying), 86/54 (standing at one minute), 81/48 
(standing at two minutes), with associated dizziness. Dose of 
midorine was increased to 10mg TID, and dose of fludrocortisone 
was increased to 0.1mg BID. Patient noticed improvement in 
symptoms, with resolution of dizziness when lying/sitting and 
less dizziness when standing. Decision was also made to 
discontinue tizanidine given the risk of hypotension secondary 
to its use. Orthostatic vital signs on discharge were; 134/75 
(lying), 104/66 (standing at one minute), 107/70 (standing at 
two minutes).

# Vaginitis vs. UTI
Patient concerned for UTI since admission. Described symptoms of 
urgency and dysuria. However, reported she has not passed urine 
over the same time period. Given repeated courses of antibiotics 
and diabetes mellitus, there was concern for candidiasis, 
although patient denied discharge, itchiness or erythema. 
Received fluconazole 150mg once for same. Passed urine following 
restarting torsemide, with no symptoms of dysuria. Urinalysis 
""dirty"" but this is to be expected. Urine culture negative with 
<10,000 CFU/ml.

# Abdominal pain
Patient with ongoing abdominal pain for several months. 
Generalized without localizing signs. Worsens during sessions of 
peritoneal dialysis. History of recurrent episodes of 
peritonitis; admitted ___ to ___ with culture negative 
peritonitis, completed antibiotics ___. Patient was 
hemodynamically stable, afebrile and WBC within normal limits 
since admission. Initial peritoneal fluid cell count was 415 
with 81% polys, concerning for underlying peritonitis. However, 
repeat count without evidence of infection. Incubation of 
peritoneal fluid culture was performed at 37C to optimize growth 
of slow-growing, fastidious organisims, which had no growth at 
time of discharge. CT abdomen/pelvis without evidence of 
abscess. Given low concern for peritonitis, and no growth on 
cultures at the time of discharge, decision was made not to 
treat with antibiotics. Abdominal pain may be secondary to 
continued peritoneal dialysis. However, patient refuses to enter 
in to discussions regarding abandoning peritoneal dialysis and 
transitioning to hemodialysis.

# T1DM
Patient with a background history of diabetes mellitus, 
complicated by ESRD, peripheral neuropathy, gastroparesis and 
likely autonomic neuropathy. Currently on transplant list for 
dual renal/pancreas transplant. Patient with complex insulin 
regimen while inpatient previously given alternate schedule for 
peritoneal dialysis, requiring ___ consultation. Continued 
home regimen of insulin glargine with insulin Humalog sliding 
scale matched to carbohydrate intake initially. Subsequently, 
reviewed by ___, who altered home insulin regimen and 
recommended standing meal time Humalog, in addition to sliding

Patient will be discharged on home regimen.

# Peritoneal dialysis
Patient with ESRD, on peritoneal dialysis for ""years"". Awaiting

remains on torsemide 100mg daily. Continued peritoneal dialysis

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with ESRD on PD c/b recent peritonitis,
admitted for persistent abdominal pain and elevated peritoneal PMN count c/f
ongoing infection// eval for abscess

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  DLP: 21.8 mGycm

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Visualized lung fields are within normal limits. There is no
evidence of pleural or pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is within normal limits.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: There is mild cortical atrophy of the bilateral kidneys.  There is no
evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no perinephric
abnormality.  A peritoneal dialysis catheter is present in the left lower
quadrant.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  The colon and
rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is not visualized.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is a
small amount of free fluid in the pelvis.  No evidence of abscess.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The uterus and bilateral adnexae are within normal
limits.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  No atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES: A small umbilical hernia containing fat is noted.

IMPRESSION:


1. No acute process in the abdomen pelvis.  Specifically, no evidence of
intra-abdominal abscess.
2. Peritoneal dialysis catheter is seen in the right lower quadrant.
